chapter_title: [Concerning the Five] War[s that the] Sons of [Li]
spiritual_reading:
The first conflict is the first direct engagement of living good with the ruling evil that arises from a full sufficiency of fundamental falsities. Living good pursued those hellish dominations by the interior power of discernment joined with affection, and by that living discernment it enclosed them within a fixed limitation so that their reasonings could no longer break out into freedom. It presented pure, uncorrupted love as an immediate witness against them, and their falsities could not discover any way to evade the restraint that true inward life imposes. Thus the whole sufficiency of their contrivances, drawn from the full series of elemental falsities, was seized and held. And living good struck at their source, removing the very origin of those organized perversions, so that the root-principle of evil was cut off with decisive force.

The second conflict is that of the living power of Divine operation that forms an ordered heaven and establishes the arrangement of truths in every degree. It disposed the rebellious dominations into their assigned states, bound them in an intermediate region, and fixed their influences within a complete arrangement of knowledges and ultimates, holding them inside the full structure of the three degrees of life. For those dominations rose up in resistance against Divine operation and set themselves against it, wishing to escape restraint because they understood that Divine power can bind and fetter by an unbreakable connection. Yet Divine operation confronted them by many modes of presence, by a fullness of ordered powers, by abundant means of action, and by severe counteraction against their violence. It made itself plainly manifest to them and, by wisdom in application, shut them in. Not one of them was able to rescue its own ruling impulse, and all their attempted evasions were brought to nothing; therefore, because their resistance was foreseen and met, they were taken in their own devices and held fast.

The third conflict is that of the mediating Divine truth that makes itself visible and operative in the lower degree. It drew up into itself all remaining good and truth that lay scattered and mixed with what devours, reclaiming every spiritual quality that had been carried off, and it laid bare the whole pretended dominion that had exalted itself by the pride of seeming light and had stretched its influence outward. Then a powerfully persuasive influx came against that dominion and stripped it of what it boasted as its own—its gathered knowledges, its falsified truths made to glitter, and its arrogance and wanton delight in dominating.

This is the nature of that pretended dominion: it claims every abundance as if it were its own, and it moves through the mind by borrowing appearances of truth and good as it passes. Therefore the mediating Divine truth purified what it had gathered, separating what is living from what is defiled, and made it clean.

The fourth conflict is that the Divine truth made fully present in the human waged against all the rebellious impulses that had risen up in interior and exterior degrees. When the reclaimed good and truth had been purified from them through the mediating revelation, the restraints that held those impulses in place began to loosen and their disorder sought to return. Then Divine truth in its glorified power came and met the uprising of the whole pretended dominion. It armed itself with the whole order of truth and good and bound the disorder again. It re-established the entire framework of spiritual life and set a great contest in which the rebellious power was brought low. In this it carried out the will of the highest Divine, and it gave hope to the first human state—hope for the preservation and eventual elevation of whatever living good and truth remained capable of being raised.

The fifth conflict is that of the living counsel that flows from the Divine, which is the inward call to what is good and the obedient reception of that call. This counsel entered with great force into the ultimate degree and set firm opposition upon the entire persuasion of spiritual death that clung to the lower life with it. And it prevailed over that persuasion forever, and it established a reign of ordered life where good governs through truth.

fills.notes: The five worlds are the canonical five realms of Darkness in the archaic cosmogony; the spiritual context speaks of “fundamental falsities” arising from a full sufficiency, i.e., the fivefold dark domains.
After “He hunted them with his net,” the next required action is enclosure: the net as living soul is the inward faculty that binds and limits hellish reasonings.
Parallel to binding: the snare is made effective by sealing, i.e., closing their outlets so they cannot break out into freedom (spiritual sense: fixed limitation).
“the face of the … his virgin” in the oldest layer is the pure witness of uncorrupted love against Darkness: the Virgin of Light, not a later devotional figure.
The living fire is the immediate manifestation of pure love; it “shines forth” as witness, and the consequence is their inability to find escape.
Causal connector: their failure to escape follows from the manifestation and constraint of the living net.
Fish-imagery regularly pairs with a dark ‘sea’ in this substrate; spiritually it is the undiscerned mass of falsities (“reasonings” as a sea).
The sentence turns from simile (“like fish”) to the capturing of the five counsels; “seized” matches the spiritual sense: “the whole sufficiency of their contrivances… was seized and held.”
After capturing the counsels, the text moves to uprooting: “cut and dug out the root…”; the demanded bridge is an explicit turn to origin or beginning (the source-principle).

fills.fill: which he waged against the rulers and the firmaments
fills.notes: The Living Spirit’s war concerns ordering and binding the rebel powers in an intermediate arrangement (firmaments, structures). This keeps the register cosmological rather than personal.
“chained them in the middle … the stars” requires the intermediate region: the firmament as middle placement between higher light and lower mixture.
“the stars in … the earths” calls for totality: the ordering fixes all influences across the arranged knowledges and ultimates.
Governance verb demanded before “them in the three vessels”: he “set” or “placed” them within the complete three-degree containment.
The rebels “wished to … since they knew… he might bind”; the required action is attempted escape from restraint.
“with numerous …” in this register is a fullness of ordered forces or powers, matching the spiritual sense “fullness of ordered powers.”
After “Not one… was able to save (himself),” the next clause must negate their evasions; “did not prevail” fits the spiritual sense that attempts were brought to nothing.
Collective subject resumes: not one saved itself, and “all of them” were nullified and imprisoned.
The spiritual translation: “because their resistance was foreseen and met”; thus the substrate clause is foreseeing their rebellion.
Correspondentially they are taken in their own contrivances; this is the fitting closure after “he trapped them …”.
The Third Ambassador “displayed his image” in the height so it can work downward (“what is below”); spiritual sense: visible operative mediation.
The motion is reclamation: drawing up scattered light; “gathered up” matches scooping and collecting in the next phrases.
Small connective restoring continuous agency of the Ambassador through the sequence of actions.
“the property … the ones that are consumed” is property stolen by the rulers and consumed in mixture; spiritual sense: carried-off spiritual qualities.
Required preposition: the light and property are reclaimed “from” the devouring ones.
Spiritual sense: “laid bare the whole pretended dominion”; thus “uncovered” is demanded.
Connects “entire ruling-power” with “pride…”; simple syntactic restoration.
“extending it …” demands a scope phrase; spiritual sense: stretched its influence outward.
The powerful person comes “against” the ruling-power to strip it; matches spiritual influx opposing dominion.
Corresponds to taking away boastful possessions; “takes his riches…” is the stripping action.
Triad “gold, silver” is conventional for apparent goods and truths in ultimates; the text already has “silver …”, so “gold” is the missing first item.
The ruling-power is described by analogy to one who claims others’ goods while passing through; “thief” corresponds to appropriating appearances of truth and good.
Explains its mode: it claims riches as its own by taking; matches spiritual sense “claims every abundance as if it were its own.”
“as they travel … light …” needs a mental topography; “paths” corresponds to ways of thought through which appearances move.
Spiritual sense: it “borrows appearances of truth and good as it passes”; thus “by borrowed” introduces those appearances.
After purification, the loosened chains lead to renewed uprising; spiritual sense: disorder sought to return.
Jesus the glorious meets rebellion and restrains it by re-binding order; “restrained” matches binding without importing later pastoral tone.
“He girded himself … all of it” in the oldest register is arming with ordered truth; correspondentially armour = defensive truths.
He girds himself and then binds the ruling-power again; required action to match “all of it another time.”
Completes “made … a great contest”: he made it firm, i.e., established the structure securely before the contest.
Accepted as fitting: the act is not devotional but structural—granting a state of expectation and preservation to the first human form.
“to his light ship” requires the object preserved and carried: the remnant of light (remaining good and truth capable of elevation).
The fifth war targets a specific opposite: the persuasive power of death-falsity; fits spiritual sense “persuasion of spiritual death.”
Balances “counsel of life … which is the summons and the obedience”; “great counsel” is the inflowing directive of order.
“great … and it placed” needs the noun: great power or force entering ultimates.
Correspondentially placing a seal is setting fixed opposition and boundary in ultimates; matches “set firm opposition.”
The counsel enters the ultimate degree; “earth” is the natural ultimate in this register.
Pairs with earth as its lowest extension; “depth” corresponds to the lowest natural level where death-persuasion clings.
“of death, which … with it” needs what death has: bonds or fetters that cling; corresponds to persuasion fastening itself to lower life.
Verb required: death’s bonds “clung with it” to the lower degree; matches spiritual translation.
Object of victory: not merely persons but the persuasive potency of death-falsity.
The conclusion “gave the kingdom …” in the oldest substrate is the reign of ordered life and light, not ecclesial language.

assessment: Most gaps can be restored to a coherent cosmological sequence because the chapter is a fivefold correspondential schema of restraint, ordering, reclamation, re-binding, and final fixation in ultimates. Exact wording at several points (especially ¶3–¶5 connectors and some locatives like “sea of smoke,” “paths,” “depth”) is less tight because the natural text is highly formulaic and could admit multiple equivalent Coptic renderings; however the demanded functions—binding, placing in the middle firmament, uncovering the pretended dominion, stripping its boast, sealing opposition in the ultimate—constrain the restorations strongly in sense and register.
